title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Doctor's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore medical knowledge through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Read the clues carefully.
Test your medical knowledge.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of medical knowledge. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, professional qualification, diagnosis or medical advice. Seek qualified medical care for personal symptoms or emergencies.

next.tagline: Up next: How the body works.

stage-10.preAdCopy: Did you reach 80%? Your score and strengths are ready.

profile-1.title: The Clinical Standout
profile-1.copy: You answered almost every question correctly. Your breakdown shows how that accuracy carried across the topics in this challenge.

profile-2.title: Strong Clinical Reasoning
profile-2.copy: You made many accurate connections across this challenge. Explore your breakdown to see which topics were strongest.

profile-3.title: The Sharp Medical Mind
profile-3.copy: You connected many of the clues and facts. Your breakdown highlights the topics you handled best and the ones worth another look.

profile-4.title: The Promising Student
profile-4.copy: You found useful clues across several topics. The answer review can help you work through the questions that caught you out.

profile-5.title: Building the Basics
profile-5.copy: Some topics were more familiar than others. Your review shows the correct answers and gives you a starting point for another attempt.

insights.overview: Your clinical score at a glance

doctor-s1q1.question: Which gas does blood pick up in the lungs?

doctor-s1q2.question: Which organs remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance?

doctor-s1q3.question: Which system carries rapid signals between the brain and the body?

doctor-s1q4.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed?

doctor-s1q5.question: Which blood cells carry most of the oxygen in blood?

doctor-s1q6.question: Which major muscle helps draw air into the lungs?

doctor-s1q7.question: Which heart chamber receives blood returning from the lungs?

doctor-s2q1.question: What is the main function of haemoglobin in red blood cells?

doctor-s2q2.question: Which hormone helps lower blood glucose by promoting uptake and storage?

doctor-s2q3.question: Which process moves water across a selectively permeable membrane?

doctor-s2q4.question: What prevents blood from flowing backwards through the heart?

doctor-s2q6.question: When body temperature rises, sweating helps cooling mainly through what?

doctor-s2q7.question: What is negative feedback in body regulation?

answers.a1: A response that opposes a change from the regulated range
answers.a2: The complete absence of a response
answers.a3: A response that always amplifies a change
answers.a4: A conscious criticism of an action

doctor-s3q1.question: Which structure contains most of the DNA in a typical human cell?

doctor-s3q3.question: What is a major role of mitochondria?

doctor-s3q4.question: What forms the main boundary of a human cell?

answers.a1: The conversion of every liquid into a gas
answers.a2: Movement that always requires a heart
answers.a4: Net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration

doctor-s3q6.question: What happens during mitosis in a typical human body cell?

answers.a1: Duplicated chromosomes are separated into two nuclei
answers.a4: Only the cell membrane is copied

doctor-s3q7.question: Which molecule carries inherited genetic instructions?

doctor-s4q1.question: An analgesic is intended primarily to reduce what?

doctor-s4q2.question: An antipyretic is used primarily to reduce what?

doctor-s4q3.question: What does a medicine’s route of administration describe?

answers.a2: A tablet is moved to a shelf
answers.a3: One substance changes the effect of another
answers.a4: Two packages have the same colour

answers.a1: The cost printed on a receipt
answers.a2: An unwanted harmful effect associated with a treatment

doctor-s4q6.question: Why distinguish a medicine’s generic name from its brand name?

answers.a1: Generic names describe only package size
answers.a2: Different brands may contain the same active ingredient
answers.a4: Every brand always contains a different ingredient

doctor-s4q7.question: A medicine label is unclear. What should happen before administration?

answers.a1: Assume all similar packages are identical
answers.a2: Clarify it through the appropriate qualified professional

doctor-s5q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a3: Put gloves on over the dirt

doctor-s5q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a1: Clean hands only if a glove tore
answers.a3: Keep the gloves for another person

doctor-s5q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a3: An open tray for later sorting

doctor-s5q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

doctor-s5q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a1: Clean it using the approved method
answers.a2: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny
answers.a3: Cover old marks with a label

doctor-s5q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a2: The contents are sterile if they look clean
answers.a3: The printed date cancels the tear

doctor-s5q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: They stay clean regardless of what they touch
answers.a2: The same pair is suitable for every patient
answers.a4: They do not replace hand hygiene

doctor-s6q2.question: What does a biopsy remove for examination?

doctor-s6q3.question: Which imaging method uses sound waves?

doctor-s6q4.question: What does a blood glucose test measure?

doctor-s6q5.question: A test has a false positive result. What does that mean?

answers.a1: It indicates a condition that is not actually present
answers.a2: It misses a condition that is present

doctor-s6q6.question: Why check the patient identifier on a specimen?

answers.a1: To replace the sample collection time
answers.a2: To predict the result from the name
answers.a3: To connect the result to the correct person

doctor-s6q7.question: A result differs sharply from earlier results and the sample label is uncertain. What needs attention?

answers.a1: The patient’s symptoms can now be ignored
answers.a2: The earlier record should be deleted
answers.a3: The sample identity and the result need verification
answers.a4: The newest number must be correct without checking

doctor-s7q1.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the record show?

answers.a1: An increase of 8 beats per minute
answers.a3: An increase of 16 beats per minute
answers.a4: A decrease of 16 beats per minute

doctor-s7q2.question: Earlier, a person spoke comfortably. Now they pause between short phrases to breathe. What changed?

answers.a2: The record proves a specific diagnosis

doctor-s7q3.question: Which observation describes a new change in alertness?

answers.a1: The chart has a new page
answers.a3: The room lights were switched on

doctor-s7q4.question: Which description records a breathing rate?

doctor-s7q5.question: What does a pulse oximeter estimate?

doctor-s7q6.question: Why should a reassuring device reading not replace assessment of new symptoms?

answers.a2: Every device always gives random values
answers.a3: One number proves all body systems are healthy
answers.a4: Measurements have limitations and need context

doctor-s7q7.question: Which change calls for prompt qualified assessment?

answers.a2: A different pen used for notes
answers.a3: New breathing difficulty with reduced alertness

doctor-s8q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a2: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions
answers.a4: Promise there is no possible risk

doctor-s8q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a3: Write the details on a public board

doctor-s8q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Treat a nod as proof of understanding
answers.a2: Ask another patient to answer for them
answers.a3: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words

doctor-s8q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: A decision made by the nearest visitor
answers.a2: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a3: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a4: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent

doctor-s8q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a1: Respect the choice and protect privacy
answers.a4: Assume silence later cancels the choice

doctor-s8q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a4: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

doctor-s8q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a4: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

doctor-s9q1.question: A record shows 700 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

doctor-s9q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

doctor-s9q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

doctor-s9q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

doctor-s9q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

doctor-s9q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

doctor-s9q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

doctor-s10q1.question: Two people have a headache. Does that alone establish the same cause?

answers.a1: Yes; if they use the same word
answers.a2: No; the same symptom can have different causes
answers.a3: Yes; each symptom has exactly one cause
answers.a4: No; symptoms can never help assessment

doctor-s10q2.question: Which is a symptom reported by a person?

answers.a1: A recorded pulse of 90 per minute
answers.a4: A visible wound described by an examiner

doctor-s10q4.question: A study finds an association between two variables. What additional claim does that alone not establish?

answers.a1: That an association was observed in the study
answers.a3: That more investigation may be useful
answers.a4: That one variable causes the other

doctor-s10q5.question: A person reports an allergy that is absent from the chart. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a2: Ignore it unless another patient agrees
answers.a3: Assume the blank chart disproves the report
answers.a4: Clarify and record the information through the care process

doctor-s10q6.question: A patient’s new symptoms conflict with a reassuring earlier note. Which information matters?

answers.a1: Only the spelling in the note
answers.a3: Both the earlier context and the new change

answers.a1: “Questions are unnecessary because a number is available”
answers.a2: “This finding has several possible causes and needs assessment”
